comparison.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks an angular-gripper stop while preserving its setting, then verifies retained motion; pr-890 drives a started bracket bolt to seated contact with a ratchet in confined access.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires simultaneous driver countertorque and thin-jam-nut wrenching on a coupled screw/nut setting, followed by functional cycling. pr-890 requires ratchet pickup, socket alignment, and repeated short drive/return strokes that advance one threaded fastener between walls.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate grades target opening accuracy, nut retention, post-lock cycle repeatability, stop drift, tool withdrawal, and clearance. The latest pr-890 spec grades axial bolt advance, actual head/bracket seating, thread integrity, and a 0.5-second seated dwell; torque and cycle counts are diagnostic, although earlier versions required six productive cycles.
comparison.reason: Both involve tools and threaded hardware, but pr-890 tests confined ratcheting to seat a fastener, whereas the candidate tests preservation of an adjustable setpoint against locknut reaction and hands-off functional retention.
